body:
Omar El-Sayed: quick question on the debug endpoint work — for the new profile pack stuff, can we add fields to /debug (and maybe /health) so on-call can see active `profile_id` + `profile_version` + detected SKU? right now it’s a lot of guesswork when someone says “H100 pool is slow”

Noah Patel: +1. We keep getting stuck at “what config is actually running”. If we can surface selection outcome in one place it’ll cut triage time a lot.

Ethan Park: where are you thinking to expose? we have:
- runtime `/health` (used by LB + some customer probes in Private)
- internal `/debug/runtime` (in Hosted/Dedicated it’s behind auth + not publicly routable)
- support bundle collector (the thing that grabs logs + env)

Omar El-Sayed: was thinking `/debug/runtime` first. maybe `/health` just gets `profile_version` so you can correlate quickly.

Benji Okafor: security angle: we should be careful what ends up in `/health` because some customers hit it / scrape it. also anything that reveals internal kernel variants, driver versions, or detailed knob values can become a fingerprinting / attack surface.

Sean Gallagher: :100: SRE perspective: whatever we expose must be safe to share in a customer ticket without us having to redact. we’ve already had “send me your /debug output” turn into a cleanup exercise.

Allison Grant: for dashboards we already plan to tag metrics with `profile_id` + `sku`. Having an endpoint that says “this node is currently on profile X” is super useful, but it should match what metrics emit (same IDs).

Kira Thompson: + doc/runbook side: we should standardize names. i’d rather we don’t expose raw knob dumps (batching thresholds, allocator params) unless it’s explicitly gated.

Noah Patel: propose split:
1) `/health`: minimal, customer-safe, stable fields
2) `/debug/runtime`: richer, internal-only (still don’t dump secrets)

Ethan Park: what’s “minimal”? i’d suggest:
- `active_profile_id` (string)
- `profile_pack_version` (string)
- `detected_gpu_sku` (H100/L40S/B200)
- `selection_source` (e.g. `default`, `fleet_override`, `customer_pin`)

Benji Okafor: `selection_source` is probably ok, but “customer_pin” might leak that a given tenant is on a non-default config? (esp in Dedicated / Private where they might not want to disclose their tuning choices internally). maybe phrase as `profile_override_present: true/false`?

Sean Gallagher: +1. For Hosted multi-tenant, we definitely should not leak anything tenant-specific via a shared endpoint. If `/health` is per-pod and not per-tenant, it’s ok, but still—avoid language that implies specific customers.

Omar El-Sayed: makes sense. so `/health` could be:
- `profile_pack_version`
- `active_profile_id`
- `detected_gpu_sku`
- `override: true/false`
no more.

Noah Patel: also add `compatibility_status` maybe? like `ok` vs `degraded` vs `blocked` (for B200 hard gate). But keep it high-level.

Ethan Park: careful: “blocked” would mean the process wouldn’t come up anyway. “degraded” might raise customer alarm if they’re scraping health.

Allison Grant: maybe `profile_status: active` only, and we leave “degraded” signals to metrics/alerts. Or put status only in /debug.

Benji Okafor: i’m ok with `profile_status` in /debug only.

Kira Thompson: +1. keep /health boring.

Connor O'Brien: release note angle: anything we add to /health becomes semi-contractual. i’d rather we add to `/debug/runtime` + support bundle first, then later decide if /health needs it.

Noah Patel: good point. /health is used by too many things. We can still add to /debug and then SRE can build a runbook “check /debug/runtime profile fields” for internal clusters.

Sean Gallagher: in Dedicated/Private, customers sometimes have direct access to debug endpoints depending on how they wire ingress. can we gate `/debug/runtime` behind an admin token / RBAC? (at least in Private installer + helm chart)

Ethan Park: for Hosted/Dedicated we already have the internal auth middleware on /debug. For Private, chart exposes it but recommended is cluster-internal only. We can add an optional `debugAuthToken` requirement in helm values, but that’s a bigger change.

Benji Okafor: minimum: ensure we don’t leak secrets. also don’t expose:
- full environment variables
- exact driver/CUDA versions
- kernel variant names (e.g. `attn_v3_flashxyz`)
- allocator internals / addresses
those can stay in logs if needed.

Omar El-Sayed: but on-call *does* need to know driver/CUDA sometimes. we’ve had profile mismatch issues.

Noah Patel: compromise: put driver/CUDA in `/debug/runtime` but only as major/minor? e.g. `cuda: 12.4`, `driver_branch: 550.x` not the full patch. and still internal-only.

Sean Gallagher: for incident triage i’d rather have full version internally. but i agree it shouldn’t be in a customer-facing endpoint.

Allison Grant: +1. metrics already have `driver_branch` label in infra inventory; we can correlate there.

Ethan Park: implement proposal:
- `/debug/runtime` response adds a `runtime_profile` section (not a full config dump) with:
  - `profile_pack_version`
  - `active_profile_id`
  - `detected_gpu_sku`
  - `override_present`
  - `selection_reason` (short string, no tenant info)
  - `cuda_version` (full)
  - `nvidia_driver_version` (full)
- `/health`: no change for now

Benji Okafor: please don’t call it “section” in the schema sense in Slack :)
But content-wise: ok, as long as it’s in debug only. Also ensure `selection_reason` can’t include raw file paths / internal hostnames.

Kira Thompson: if we do this, can we also add it to the “standard on-call debug bundle” doc? we have an internal request open for “active profile in debug bundle” (INT-8831 i think).

Omar El-Sayed: yep that’s the one. i’ll link when i find it.

Connor O'Brien: timeline: if this lands pre-1.22 cut, it needs to be behind the same feature flag as profile pack or at least not break older runtimes.

Ethan Park: it can be additive fields; older consumers ignore. should be safe.

Noah Patel: action items:
- Ethan: add fields to `/debug/runtime` (internal only) and make sure they’re redacted/safe
- Benji: quick review on wording/fields for security
- Kira/Sean: update runbook snippet “where to look” once it merges

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: please also log a single line on startup with active profile and sku so we can see it in plain logs when debug is blocked.

Omar El-Sayed: +1. we already talked about a startup summary log in another PR; this ties in.

Benji Okafor: final note: ensure the endpoint doesn’t dump *effective* knob values. that’s where most fingerprinting risk is.

Ethan Park: ack. will keep it to identifiers + versions + detected hardware. will open PR and tag folks.

Connor O'Brien: when PR is up, drop link here. also add a small note to the release checklist that we intentionally did NOT change /health.

Allison Grant: and please keep the field names consistent with metrics tags: `profile_id` vs `active_profile_id` — pick one and stick.

Noah Patel: i vote `profile_id` + `profile_pack_version` everywhere.

Ethan Park: ok: `profile_id`, `profile_pack_version`, `gpu_sku`, `override_present`, `cuda_version`, `nvidia_driver_version`.

Kira Thompson: works. i’ll mirror in docs.

Sean Gallagher: thanks. this will save us hours next time :)
